**Original Question:**
What are the IATA codes for the US major airports, as classified by the US Department of Transportation, which saw improvements of at least one ranking position of their On-Time Arrival Rankings from the 2023 calendar year to the 2024 calendar year, where the on time percentage in 2024 was at least 77.0% and no greater than 81.5%? Use Bureau of Transportation Statistics for data.

**Previous Reasoning Steps:**
[turn 1] We need to find US major airports classified by US DOT, presumably "Major Hubs" category or similar. We need on-time arrival rankings 2023 and 2024, from BLS (Bureau of Transportation Statistics). Need those that improved ranking position (i.e., rank number decreased? Usually ranking 1 is best. So improvement means lower numeric rank). Need 2024 on-time percentage between 77.0% and 81.5% inclusive.

We must provide IATA codes of those airports.

We must browse BTS data.

Search web.

[turn 2] We need BTS On-Time Arrival Rankings for major US airports for 2023 and 2024, and find those with improvement (rank decreased number i.e., better), at least one ranking position improvement. Condition: 2024 on time percentage between 77.0% and 81.5% inclusive? At least 77.0% and no greater than 81.5%. Also need IATA codes of those airports.

We need to find dataset pages: "Annual On-Time Arrival Rankings for Major Airports" likely gives each year with ranking and on time percentage. Need to check 2023 and 2024 tables.

Let's fetch that.

## Airline On-Time Statistics

**NOTE: Data are available from January 1995 through **June 2026**. Times are reported in local time using a 24 hour clock.**  
**Reporting changes due to mergers.** Joint reporting begins after Federal Aviation Administration approval of a single operating certificate.

*    Jan. 2006: **US Airways (US)** and **America West (HP)** start to report jointly as **US Airways (US)**. 
*    Jan. 2010: **Delta (DL)** and **Northwest (NW)** start to report jointly as **Delta (DL)**. 
*    Jan. 2012: **United (UA)** and **Continental (CO)** start to report jointly as **United (UA)**. 
*    Jan. 2012: **Atlantic Southeast (EV)** and **ExpressJet (XE)** start to report jointly as **ExpressJet (EV)**, presented here as **ExpressJet Combined (E*)**.   
 For data through Dec. 31, 2011, use the code **EV** for **Atlantic Southeast** and the code **XE** for **ExpressJet**.   
 Beginning with January 1, 2012 data, use the code **E*** for **ExpressJet Combined**. Searches for EV or XE will find data for the period ending Dec. 31, 2011 only. Searches for E* will find data for the period beginning Jan. 1, 2012 only. 
*    Aug. 2013: **Pinnacle (9E)** changed name to **Endeavor**. 
*    Apr. 2014: **American Eagle (MQ)** changed name to **Envoy**. 
*    Jan. 2015: **Southwest (WN)** and **AirTran (FL)** start to report jointly as **Southwest (WN)**. 
*    Jul. 2015: **American (AA)** and **US Airways (US)** start to report jointly as **American (AA)**. 
*    Apr. 2018: **Alaska (AS) and Virgin America (VX) start to report jointly as Alaska (AS)**.

Airline on-time data are reported in 2021 to the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) by the 17 U.S.[air carriers](https://www.bts.dot.gov/explore-topics-and-geography/topics/airline-time-performance-and-causes-flight-delays) that have at least 0.5 percent of total domestic scheduled-service passenger revenues.

*   [Regularly Scheduled Flights Canceled 5% or More](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/ONTIME/5PctCancels.aspx)

## Airline On-Time Statistics

**NOTE: Data are available from January 1995 through **June 2026**. Times are reported in local time using a 24 hour clock.**  
**Reporting changes due to mergers.** Joint reporting begins after Federal Aviation Administration approval of a single operating certificate.

*    Jan. 2006: **US Airways (US)** and **America West (HP)** start to report jointly as **US Airways (US)**. 
*    Jan. 2010: **Delta (DL)** and **Northwest (NW)** start to report jointly as **Delta (DL)**. 
*    Jan. 2012: **United (UA)** and **Continental (CO)** start to report jointly as **United (UA)**. 
*    Jan. 2012: **Atlantic Southeast (EV)** and **ExpressJet (XE)** start to report jointly as **ExpressJet (EV)**, presented here as **ExpressJet Combined (E*)**.   
 For data through Dec. 31, 2011, use the code **EV** for **Atlantic Southeast** and the code **XE** for **ExpressJet**.   
 Beginning with January 1, 2012 data, use the code **E*** for **ExpressJet Combined**. Searches for EV or XE will find data for the period ending Dec. 31, 2011 only. Searches for E* will find data for the period beginning Jan. 1, 2012 only. 
*    Aug. 2013: **Pinnacle (9E)** changed name to **Endeavor**. 
*    Apr. 2014: **American Eagle (MQ)** changed name to **Envoy**. 
*    Jan. 2015: **Southwest (WN)** and **AirTran (FL)** start to report jointly as **Southwest (WN)**. 
*    Jul. 2015: **American (AA)** and **US Airways (US)** start to report jointly as **American (AA)**. 
*    Apr. 2018: **Alaska (AS) and Virgin America (VX) start to report jointly as Alaska (AS)**.

Airline on-time data are reported in 2021 to the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) by the 17 U.S.[air carriers](https://www.bts.dot.gov/explore-topics-and-geography/topics/airline-time-performance-and-causes-flight-delays) that have at least 0.5 percent of total domestic scheduled-service passenger revenues.
